correctness.rationale: Wick/Isserlis pairing gives Δ=2(a²+b²+c²)+8abc=2S+8P for standardized centered jointly Gaussian triples. PSD determinant 1+2P−S>=0 and AM-GM |P|<=(S/3)^{3/2} yield P>=max((S−1)/2, −(S/3)^{3/2}), crossing only at S=3/4. The a=b=t,c=−t matrix is PSD for t<=1/2 and attains the lower branch; a=b=t,c=2t²−1 is singular PSD for t∈[1/2,1], maps monotonically over S∈[3/4,3] and attains the upper branch. Equality classes follow from strict AMGM/determinant. Minimizing Δ/S on the two branches yields sharp 2/3 at S=3/4 and Δ=0 at independence. Independent exact symbolic/rational checks corroborate endpoint, PSD and equality; proof works for all singular and nonsingular Gaussian correlation matrices.

evidence: Herry–Malicet–Poly Theorem1.1 proves Δ>=0 (and analogous all-even exponent statements); Hu–Zhao–Zhou 2023 prove quantitative bivariate inequalities and ask explicitly for 3D.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A qualitative ≥0 theorem for any exponent cannot imply the sharp positive lower function of S or its equality classes except at S=0; broader exponent hypotheses do not provide stronger correlation-dependent conclusions.
